quickSummary.coreConcept: IFRS 16 requires lessees to recognize nearly all leases on the balance sheet as a Right-of-Use (ROU) Asset and a Lease Liability. This eliminates the distinction between operating and finance leases for lessees, ensuring transparency of lease obligations. The standard applies to all leases except short-term leases (<12 months) and low-value assets (<$5,000).
keyFormulas: Initial Lease Liability = Present Value of Lease Payments (PV = PMT × Annuity Factor)
Right-of-Use Asset = Initial Lease Liability + Initial Direct Costs + Prepayments - Lease Incentives
Depreciation Expense = ROU Asset ÷ Lease Term (straight-line)
Interest Expense = Lease Liability × Implicit Interest Rate (or Incremental Borrowing Rate)
Annual Lease Payment = PMT = (Principal × Rate) / (1 - (1 + Rate)^-n)

commonExamTraps: Using the wrong discount rate: Must use the rate implicit in the lease if available; otherwise use the lessee's incremental borrowing rate
Forgetting to add initial direct costs to ROU Asset: These are NOT expensed immediately
Mixing up depreciation period: Use the SHORTER of lease term or useful life (unless purchase option is reasonably certain)
Ignoring residual value guarantees: Include in lease liability if probable payment
Variable lease payments tied to an index/rate: Include in liability, reassess when index changes

mnemonics.name: ROU-GLI
mnemonics.description: ROU Asset = Liability + Guarantees + Initial costs - Incentives. Remember the GLI (Good Lessee Includes) formula

mnemonics.name: SLIDE
mnemonics.description: Short-term exemption, Low-value exemption, Insurance not included, Depreciate ROU, Interest on liability

mustMemorizeRules: Short-term lease exemption: ≤12 months (no renewal options counted) → expense straight-line
Low-value asset exemption: < $5,000 fair value (e.g., laptops, office furniture) → expense straight-line
Depreciation of ROU: Straight-line over lease term (or useful life if shorter)
Interest calculation: Reducing balance on the lease liability, NOT on the ROU asset
Statement of Cash Flows: Principal portion = financing activity; Interest portion = operating (or financing under IAS 7 choice)

quickSummary.coreConcept: IAS 36 ensures that assets are carried at no more than their recoverable amount. When an asset's carrying amount exceeds its recoverable amount (higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use), an impairment loss must be recognized. The standard requires annual impairment testing for goodwill, intangibles with indefinite lives, and intangibles not yet available for use.
keyFormulas: Recoverable Amount = Higher of (Fair Value Less Costs of Disposal, Value in Use)
Impairment Loss = Carrying Amount - Recoverable Amount
Value in Use = Sum of Discounted Future Cash Flows (PV = Σ [CF / (1+r)^t])
Cash-Generating Unit (CGU) Impairment: Allocate loss to goodwill first, then other assets pro-rata
Reversal Limit: Cannot reverse impairment on goodwill (ever) or above original cost for other assets

commonExamTraps: Wrong ordering of impairment allocation: MUST allocate to goodwill FIRST, then to other CGU assets pro-rata
Confusing corporate assets with CGU assets: Corporate assets (e.g., headquarters) need special allocation before impairment
Forgetting the recoverable amount is the HIGHER of the two values: Many students pick the lower
Not testing goodwill annually: Goodwill MUST be tested for impairment every year, regardless of indicators
Ignoring the value in use discount rate: Must use pre-tax discount rate reflecting current market assessments

mnemonics.name: VU-FV-CD
mnemonics.description: Value in Use, Fair Value, Costs of Disposal — recoverable amount is the MAX of VU and FV-CD

mnemonics.name: GOW-PRO
mnemonics.description: Goodwill first, Other assets Weighted pro-rata — the impairment allocation sequence

mustMemorizeRules: Annual impairment test required: Goodwill, intangibles with indefinite useful lives, intangibles not yet available for use
Impairment indicators: External (market decline, adverse changes) and Internal (obsolescence, restructuring)
Goodwill impairment reversal: PROHIBITED under IAS 36
Other asset impairment reversal: Permitted up to the lower of (recoverable amount, carrying amount without prior impairment)
Discount rate for value in use: Must be pre-tax rate reflecting time value of money and asset-specific risks

notes.title: DEAD CLIC: The Double Entry Framework

quickSummary.coreConcept: DEAD CLIC is the fundamental mnemonic for understanding debits and credits in double-entry bookkeeping. It classifies accounts into two groups: DEAD (Debits increase Expenses, Assets, Drawings) and CLIC (Credits increase Liabilities, Income, Capital). Every transaction must have equal debits and credits, maintaining the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
keyFormulas: Expanded Equation: Assets + Expenses = Liabilities + Equity + Revenue
Debit Entry = Increase in DEAD items OR Decrease in CLIC items
Credit Entry = Increase in CLIC items OR Decrease in DEAD items
Trial Balance: Total Debits = Total Credits (must always balance)

commonExamTraps: Confusing debit/credit with increase/decrease: The side depends on the account type
Forgetting contra entries: Sales returns → debit sales returns (contra to sales), not debit sales
Drawing vs Dividend: Drawings are debits (DEAD), Dividends declared are debits to Retained Earnings
Accumulated depreciation: This is a CREDIT balance (contra-asset), not a debit
Bank overdrafts: Credit balance in bank account — it's a liability, not an asset

mnemonics.name: DEAD
mnemonics.description: Debits increase Expenses, Assets, Drawings — these accounts have normal debit balances

mnemonics.name: CLIC
mnemonics.description: Credits increase Liabilities, Income, Capital — these accounts have normal credit balances

mnemonics.name: PEARS
mnemonics.description: Purchases, Expenses, Assets have normal Debit balance; Revenue, Sales, Liabilities have normal Credit balance

mustMemorizeRules: Every transaction has equal debits and credits
Assets + Expenses = Liabilities + Equity + Revenue (always balanced)
Normal balance: Assets/Expenses = Debit; Liabilities/Equity/Revenue = Credit
Contra accounts: Accumulated depreciation (credit contra-asset), Sales returns (debit contra-revenue)
Cash book: Debit = money in (asset increase), Credit = money out (asset decrease)
